hero.title: Analyses
hero.description: Texts produced from Delivery Worker Atlas data, bringing together interpretation of results, dialogue with workers, research, and reflection on platform work.

items.title: How much is one hour of a delivery worker's labor worth?
items.summary: An analysis of hourly earnings considering expenses, idle time, and effective working time. The results show how costs and variability in demand affect delivery workers' real remuneration.

items.title: Does working more mean earning more?
items.summary: An examination of the relationship between working-time duration, waiting time, and delivery workers' net income. The results show that more hours do not always translate into higher earnings because of idle time and activity costs.

items.title: The weight of expenses in app-based work
items.summary: A look at everyday costs such as fuel, food, maintenance, and internet in the budgets of platform workers. The analysis shows how expenses affect final income and the sustainability of the activity.

items.title: Maps of circulation: mobility, territory, and platforms
items.summary: An interpretation of urban movements, areas of concentration, and territorial inequalities based on geolocation data. The results point to an unequal distribution of opportunities among different parts of the city.

items.title: Who are the workers represented in the Atlas?
items.summary: A reading of participants' demographic profile and the differences observed among cities, vehicles, and platforms. The analysis reveals the diversity of profiles and the inequalities that shape platform work in Brazil.

article.title: How much is one hour of a delivery worker's labor worth?
article.subtitle: Hourly earnings change significantly when expenses, idle time, and effective working time are taken into account.

heroImage.alt: Delivery worker riding through a city at sunset

introParagraphs: Digital platform delivery workers are a central part of the contemporary urban economy. They connect restaurants, businesses, and consumers, ensuring the operation of a system that has expanded rapidly in recent years. Yet the earnings obtained by these workers are still not very transparent and are often analyzed only in terms of gross values, without considering expenses, idle time, and the effective duration of the working day.

In this analysis, we use data collected by Delivery Worker Atlas between 2024 and 2026 to estimate how much delivery workers really earn per hour, considering different vehicle types, cities, and platforms. The results show that net hourly remuneration is significantly lower than gross figures suggest and varies according to vehicle type, city, and platform.

sections.title: How much do delivery workers earn per hour?
paragraphs: Average hourly remuneration varies according to the type of vehicle used. When we consider only gross earnings, the values appear higher. However, after deducting expenses and idle time, net hourly remuneration is significantly lower.

chart.title: Hourly remuneration by vehicle type
chart.subtitle: Mean and median values (R$), considering net earnings.
chart.source: Delivery Worker Atlas. Data from Jan/2024 – Jul/2026.

afterChartParagraphs: The difference between mean and median values also indicates substantial heterogeneity among workers, with some receiving amounts far below the average. These results reinforce the importance of analyzing remuneration by considering the full set of factors that make up the working day.
